chain.label: Night approach in darkness
chain.trigger: The accident occurred about 2341 during hours of darkness

chain.label: Malfunction occurred about 200 feet above the approach lights on short final
chain.trigger: When the airplane was about 200 feet over the approach lights, an increase in engine thrust was heard

chain.label: Undetermined defect in the right spoiler system
chain.trigger: The Safety Board could not determine the reason for the right spoiler malfunction

chain.label: Spoiler warning light not illuminated, possibly inoperative
chain.trigger: the light bulb or wiring may have been defective and that the system was not operative

chain.label: Spoilers extended in the turn to final and left extended as gear and flaps were lowered
chain.trigger: The pilot of Night Air 4 extended spoilers during the turn to the final approach and inadvertently did not retract them until over the approach lights

chain.label: Crew did not recognize the spoilers were still extended on final approach
chain.trigger: the spoilers extended configuration only requires 3 percent more power than retracted configuration and a pilot could overlook the difference in power particularly if the spoiler warning lights were not lit

caused_by.evidence: the Safety Board believes that the spoilers were still extended
If the system was inoperative, it would further explain why the flightcrew did not notice the extended spoilers on the final approach
there is little difference in cockpit total background noise level with spoilers either extended or retracted when the gear and flaps are down to alert the pilot

chain.label: Asymmetric spoiler retraction: left spoiler retracted, right spoiler did not
chain.trigger: an asymmetric retraction of the flight spoilers wherein the left spoiler retracted and the right spoiler did not

caused_by.evidence: as the airplane passed over the approach lights, the pilot realized that the spoilers were extended and retracted them
The right spoiler actuator was recovered in an extended position, and the left actuator in a retracted position

chain.label: Pilot added power and used aileron trim but applied insufficient aileron and rudder to arrest the roll
chain.trigger: While the pilot added power, he apparently did not use enough aileron and rudder control input to arrest the roll

caused_by.evidence: indicates that the pilot attempted to counteract an uncommanded airplane roll to the right by using aileron trim

If an asymmetrical spoiler condition were to occur at night on final approach, airplane roll rates might develop to a degree that delayed recovery inputs by an unwary pilot would not be sufficient to stop the roll
the flight tests were made under controlled conditions at altitude with forewarning of the conditions

chain.label: Uncommanded roll to the right through about 90 degrees with nose drop
chain.trigger: an uncommanded roll to the right which caused the airplane to roll about 90 degrees and descend into the ground

caused_by.evidence: The spoilers did not retract symmetrically causing the airplane to roll to the right
the pilot apparently did not detect the roll before the roll rate developed to the extent that the airplane could not be controlled

chain.label: Nose-low ground impact 1,200 feet right of the runway 33 threshold and postimpact fire
chain.trigger: The airplane's nose dropped below the horizon and the airplane descended into the ground in a nose low attitude

caused_by.evidence: the airplane rolled inverted and crashed

chain.label: Both pilots and the passenger killed
chain.trigger: Both pilots and the one passenger on board were killed

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable because impact forces exceeded human tolerances
